- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling), model often fails to correct; reduce forecast slope.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out forecast by averaging last 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; match forecast to sentiment trend, not absolute value.
- When true outcome is below 65, model often overpredicts; apply downward bias of 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or weak.
